arm_frames.note: SO-101 bimanual — per-arm base frames, NOT a shared world frame

sensor_semantics.arm_frames: Each arm's translations are expressed in ITS OWN base (mounting) frame, computed by forward kinematics from that arm's joint angles: • +X = forward, i.e. away from THAT arm's own base along its reach • +Y = left of that arm's base • +Z = up Consequences: - Direction words describe each arm's motion relative to its own base. "L arm moves 5 cm forward" and "R arm moves 5 cm forward" are not necessarily the same direction in the room. - Left and right arm positions live in different frames, so they cannot be subtracted or compared: never infer the distance between the two grippers, which arm is further left, or whether they are about to collide from these numbers. Use the overhead view for anything that involves both arms at once, or absolute workspace layout. - Absolute FK error is ≈1–2 cm; treat small offsets as noise and read the numbers for their trend, not their absolute value.
sensor_semantics.translation_per_phase: - "N cm forward/backward/left/right/up/down" — net displacement components in that arm's own base frame (end-of-phase pose minus start-of-phase pose). - "path N cm" — arc length = sum of frame-to-frame distances over the phase (always ≥ |net displacement|). path ≫ |displacement| means the arm did not follow a straight trajectory.

rotation_per_phase.format: "X arm wrist: net N°, total N°, stability S"

sensor_semantics.rotation_per_phase: - "net N°" — magnitude of net rotation: the single equivalent rotation angle from start orientation to end orientation. - "total N°" — cumulative angular path: sum of |frame-to-frame rotation magnitudes| over the phase. total ≥ net always; equality means the rotation was monotonic. - "stability S ∈ [0,1]" — axis-consistency = how concentrated the instantaneous rotation axis is across the phase. S = 1 → every step shares the same axis and sign (single-axis monotonic motion). S < 1 → axis switched directions, or different steps used different axes, or both. A +X°-then-−X° reversal drives S toward 0. - If net + total < 5° (effectively no rotation), the wrist line is omitted from that phase entirely. - Practical reading: small translation path + large total + high stability → an active wrist-driven rotation (pour / tilt / turn). Large total alongside large translation path usually means the wrist is dragged by the arm sweep, not an active turn.
